aiExplanation: This function checks whether every `'a'` in the string `s` appears **before** every `'b'`, which is the same as saying no `'a'` ever comes after a `'b'`. It walks through the string one character at a time while tracking a single boolean flag, `hasSeenB`, that starts as `false` and flips to `true` the first time a `'b'` is encountered. Since the string only contains `'a'` and `'b'`, any character that is **not** `'b'` must be an `'a'`, so if the flag is already `true` when an `'a'` shows up, the order has been broken and the function immediately returns `false`. If the loop finishes without ever hitting that case, all the `'a'`s came first and it returns `true`. The approach runs in **O(n)** time with **O(1)** extra space because it makes a single pass and remembers only one flag.
